title: Line Follower Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js top-down simulation of a two-sensor line-following robot running the Chapter 10 adjust_motors() rules on oval, figure-8, and zigzag tracks. Students tune the fast duty, slow duty, and update rate, watch the active sensor state in a four-row table, and measure time on the line and the tightest turn radius.

educational.topic: Line following with dual IR sensors and motor differential adjust
learningObjectives: Explain how each of the four IR sensor states maps to left and right motor duties
Explain why slowing the wheel on the line side steers the robot back onto the line
Predict what happens when the slow duty is too close to the fast duty (weak correction)
Predict what happens when the fast speed is too high for the update rate
prerequisites: Chapter 10 dual IR sensor reading and adjust_motors()

controls.label: Reset robot
controls.purpose: Put the robot back on the start of the line and clear the statistics

controls.label: Fast speed (duty)
controls.purpose: FULL in adjust_motors(); snaps to steps of 1000

controls.label: Slow speed (duty)
controls.purpose: HALF in adjust_motors(); never above the fast speed

controls.label: Update rate (Hz)
controls.purpose: How often the loop reads the sensors (1 / sleep time)

simulation.modelType: Kinematic differential-drive simulation with sampled sensors
equations: tightest turn radius = 6 x (fast + slow) / (fast - slow) cm
assumptions: The line is 4 cm wide and the sensors are 4 cm apart on the front edge
A sensor reads LOW when it is within 2 cm of the line center
Motors keep their last duty between updates
limitations: No wheel slip, motor mismatch, or sensor noise
Sensors are perfectly calibrated for the floor and lighting

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Running simulation with parameter sliders, live state table, and readouts
keyQuestions: When the left sensor reads LOW, which wheel slows down and which way does the robot turn?
Why does the robot lose the zigzag track with the default slow speed?
How far does the robot travel between sensor readings at 10 Hz?
What should the robot do when both sensors read HIGH?
commonMisconceptions: Lowering the fast speed always helps (it can weaken the turn if the slow speed stays the same)
The robot steers toward the side of the faster wheel
The loop rate does not matter if the motors are fast
assessmentOpportunities: Data table of slow speed, tightest turn, and time on line
Largest working fast speed at 50, 20, and 10 Hz
Exit ticket proposing two fixes for a robot that loses sharp corners
